title: Anacav
excerpt: My interview at Anacav was great, but low salary and a position far from my expertise made me walk away.

blocks.text: The Pooyan Novin Big Data Company, or Anacav, is located in the science and research center at Isfahan University of Technology. It's safe to say it was my best interview experience to date.

I used the Job Vision platform to send my resume. They called me and invited me for an interview for a Data Engineer position. I had learned from previous interviews and prepared more than before, reviewing the basic concepts so I wouldn't forget them.

Finding their place was a bit hard and I had to ask people for the name and location of the building several times, but I found it anyway :) By the way, they had sent me the exact address and location themselves.

When I went, they were waiting for me and I arrived 2 minutes late. They put a form in front of me to fill out and that was a buzzkill - why? Because I had given you my resume! All this information was in my resume! Anyway, it was just a form and I filled in the information - again, no big deal, it was tolerable.

My interview was with two women - though I didn't understand their positions at the company - but it was a very good interview. They asked two or three basic technical questions about databases and such, and then went to questions outside the field. What's your goal - where do you see your future - how many supermarkets do you think there are in Iran? - do you want to immigrate or not - what's your expectation from the company? - what drives you crazy and makes you angry? - if you have a project and the deadline has passed, how do you talk to explain it and...
I also just bring a happy game vibe to the interview atmosphere, it was really good and the vibe was very positive.

I had written my requested salary as 40 million tomans, but as far as I understood they would give me at most 25 to 30 million tomans because my work experience was low, which I found unacceptable, because their location was really far from me.
They themselves said the average time people stay at this company is 1 year, but in my opinion it's less, at most 6-7 months.

Anyway, their situation was good and they had 200+ contracts with electricity and water companies and such. They did their work. But in the end the Data Engineering position turned into working with Lakehouse and this was annoying for me and my expertise and the work I had done so far.

In the end they told me I had to do a test project and I had 10 days, I had to come and present. This project was some data that we had to analyze in a database and build a dashboard and present. What was important to them was my perspective on the data and the analyses I presented.

Considering the conditions, the distance of the workplace, the very low salary, and the position being far from my expertise, I decided not to do this work and announced my withdrawal from the process.

Definitely yes - in my opinion out of 10, it can be given a 6.5. The environment was good and the work was good too but it depended on people's conditions. For me it wasn't worth it but it was really a good place to work. They were very good. I hope they are always successful.
